summary.text: Early forms are interpreted as a foot above a person, conveying going ahead. Shang inscriptions attest both precedence and leading uses; their order and semantic connection remain unresolved.

formation.text: A proposed early construction combines two pictorial elements: a foot above a person, showing someone stepping ahead. Its connection to the modern graph is unresolved. The later 說文 account instead analyzes 先 as 从儿从之; transmitted editions differ on the first component, so this account does not settle the earlier construction.

components.text: In the proposed Shang analysis, 止 depicts a foot and contributes the action of stepping ahead. Early forms are broadly described with it above a person, though its graphic continuity into modern 先 is unresolved.
The proposed Shang analysis identifies a person as 人 beneath the foot. Modern 先 has 儿 in this position, but the precise graphic relationship between early 人 and visible 儿 remains unresolved.

history.text: The paleographic account groups early forms under oracle-bone, bronze, Chu-slip and small-seal categories and broadly describes a person below a foot. It does not document a complete sequence of changes into the modern graph.
The received 說文 gives a different analysis, 从儿从之. Transmitted editions differ between 几 and 儿; this later dictionary account does not directly establish the earliest construction.
A study distinguishes the Shang graph read as 先 from a similar-looking graph with disputed readings such as 失 or 姺. That separate identification dispute does not show that 先 itself is corrupted.

uncertainties.text: The proposed person-and-foot construction is supported for early forms, but its exact graphic continuity into modern 先 remains unresolved; the received 說文 account differs from the Shang analysis.

Shang-period precedence and going-ahead or leading uses are both attested, but their relative priority and semantic connection are unresolved. The later meanings “former” and “previous” are recorded, but their development from those Shang uses is not established.

senses.gloss: precedence; first or earlier in time or order
senses.text: Shang oracle-bone examples use 先 for temporal or ordered precedence, including in references to ancestors, wine and years. They are dated broadly by corpus context, not by individual artifact dates.

Shang oracle-bone examples use 先 for going ahead or leading in hunting and military contexts. It is attested in the same broad period as precedence, but the evidence does not establish which use came first.
“Former” and “previous” are recorded meanings of 先. Their chronology and connection to the Shang uses are unresolved.

limitations.text: The evidence attests both precedence and going-ahead uses in Shang contexts, but does not establish their relative priority or a semantic path to the later meanings “former” and “previous.”

overview.text: An early analysis combines a foot above a person to express going ahead. Shang inscriptions attest both precedence and leading, while modern 先 means “first” or “earlier”; the order of the two Shang uses is unresolved.

components.text: The proposed early analysis treats 止 as a foot, contributing the action of stepping ahead; its connection to the modern graph is unresolved.
The proposed analysis identifies a person beneath the foot; modern 先 has 儿 here, but its graphic connection to 人 is unresolved.

relationships.text: The proposed Shang analysis identifies 止 as a foot, consistent with the broad account of early forms describing a foot above a person and conveying going ahead.
The proposed Shang analysis identifies a person as 人 beneath the foot; the modern visible form is 儿, but their precise graphic connection is unresolved.
